summary: Pass 41 promotes the broad Classic error-handling/recovery assertion to STRONG by separating ordinary state-preserving gameplay rejection from catastrophic native-file/startup failure and Reforged-owned transactional recovery. Exact native failure wording and catastrophic save rollback ordering remain unresolved.
classificationPolicy: PASS requires exact native branch behavior and presentation; operator-confirmed/state-preserving gameplay rejection may support executable STRONG/PASS-narrow subcontracts without inventing command text or catastrophic persistence ordering.

facts.claim: An ordinary rejected Classic gameplay action leaves gameplay state unchanged and does not invoke synthetic rollback/recovery.
evidence: Project-owner/operator Classic behavior retained in Pass 33
runtime: Pass 41 verifies Apply does not disable the gameplay subsystem even when rollback is nominally available.

facts.claim: Wrong/corrupt or wrong-version native MajorMUD files belong to a hard startup/load failure boundary, not the ordinary rejected-gameplay no-op path.
runtime: World-load-critical recovery stops load; RuntimeImportExportCompatibility enforces exact Classic file/version replacement boundaries.

facts.claim: Exact native failure text versus silent no-op is command/action-specific.
facts.boundary: No generic synthetic Classic error text is promoted.

facts.claim: Exact behavior when a malformed/missing MajorMUD data reference is reached after successful startup remains unresolved.
facts.boundary: Do not assume every such failure crashes Worldgroup and do not assume graceful recovery.

facts.claim: Exact native save participant/rollback ordering on catastrophic persistence failure remains unresolved.
facts.boundary: Separate from the proven 60-second save interval and from ordinary gameplay rejection.

facts.claim: Reforged rollback helpers used for internal atomicity do not prove a native MajorMUD ordinary-gameplay rollback subsystem.

parityPromotion.reason: The major ownership branches are now evidence-separated and executable: ordinary gameplay rejection is state-preserving, incompatible native files are catastrophic startup/load failures, and synthetic Reforged rollback is not treated as native evidence. Exact presentation and catastrophic save ordering remain open.
